summary: Alert escalation chain and tracehook parameters cleared during hourly retention rollforward
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that alert escalation recipients and tracehook URL parameters are being cleared for saved alerts when a scheduled hourly retention rollforward job runs on the metrics/usage index. This appears to affect alerts that reference tracehooks (dashboard trace links) and alerts whose escalation chain included external webhook targets.

Impact:
- For BrightLens (enterprise customer) several alerts did not notify downstream paging targets during 2026-03-10 01:00-02:30 UTC window.
- Trace links from affected dashboard time ranges no longer contain the org-scoped tracehook token, making drilldown links return 403 or broken trace contexts.
- Customer reported missed escalation to on-call (PagerDuty) for a P1 spike.

Environment:
- Redwood console, prod, us-east region.
- Affected alert types: composite metric alerts and scheduled anomaly alerts with tracehook enabled.

Observed behaviour:
- After the hourly rollforward job completes, alert rule configuration entries show empty arrays for escalation recipients and tracehook_params in the persisted alert document.
- The UI still shows the pre-rollforward escalation list for ~5-10 minutes until a full refresh, but the backend evaluates the empty list and does not send notifications.

Steps to reproduce (attempted by Support and reproduced in staging):
1) Create a composite alert on console using a high-cardinality metric with an attached tracehook (org token).
2) Configure an escalation chain: webhooks -> PagerDuty -> email. Save rule.
3) Wait for the scheduled hourly retention rollforward job to run (simulate by running rollforward script in staging).
4) Trigger the alert condition.
5) Observe that no webhooks/PagerDuty notifications are sent and dashboard trace link returns 403 or trace ID missing.

Initial logs and evidence:
- API audit entry (alerts service) before rollforward: alert_config_id=abf-12ec; escalation_targets=[pd:PD-abc, webhook:https://hooks.example.com/bf]
- API audit entry after rollforward: alert_config_id=abf-12ec; escalation_targets=[]
- Console UI trace: GET /api/alerts/abf-12ec returned escalationTargets: [] at 2026-03-10T01:03:14Z
- Customer-reported incident ID: BL-INC-20260310-01

Notes about scope:
- This is not the same as missing alert deliveries caused by transient downstream failure; the persisted rule state itself is mutated.
- Affected customers are limited to orgs that have had historical index compactions and hourly rollforward enabled (enterprise/dedicated accounts with high ingestion).
steps_to_reproduce: Create composite alert with tracehook and escalation recipients in prod/staging console.
Ensure hourly retention rollforward job is scheduled or run the rollforward script manually in staging.
Trigger the alert and observe notification delivery and trace link behavior before and after the rollforward run.
Compare alert_config documents in the alerts service DB pre- and post-rollforward (watch escalationTargets and tracehookParams fields).
logs: 2026-03-10T00:59:02Z alerts-service INFO Persisted alert abf-12ec with escalationTargets=[pd:PD-abc, webhook:https://hooks.example.com/bf]
2026-03-10T01:02:47Z retention-worker INFO Starting hourly rollforward for org=brightlens, index=usage-v2
2026-03-10T01:03:12Z alerts-service WARN Updated alert abf-12ec: escalationTargets=[] (source=rollforward job migration)
2026-03-10T01:04:05Z console-proxy ERROR Tracehook lookup failed for token=null for alert abf-12ec
investigation_notes: Support reproduced behavior in staging by running hourly rollforward script against a copy of customer's alerts DB snapshot.

Hypothesis: rollforward migration job applies a schema normalization step that overwrites nested recipient arrays when encountering high-cardinality target metadata; related to recent retention compact rewrite (PR #2289).

DB diff shows that migration pipeline writes a transformed alert document where 'escalationTargets' is initialised from an intermediary map that is empty for webhook+pd entries when non-legacy target metadata present.
Retention worker logs show 'migration:normalize_targets' step executed at 2026-03-10T01:03:10Z for org brightlens - correlates with updated_at on alert document.
Tracehook tokens are stored as namespaced parameters on the alert document; migration attempted to dedupe repeated tokens and dropped them when it encountered duplicate token hash collision.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:10 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Customer reports missed PagerDuty page during spike; escalated to SRE. Attached example alert_config id and timestamps.
2026-03-10 03:05 - Martin O'Neill (SRE): I reproduced in staging. I've flagged migration step 'normalize_targets' as suspect. Collecting DB diffs and trace of the retention worker run.

2026-03-10 09:22 - Lina Park (Platform Eng): Found PR #2289 changed the migration input for target mappings; looks like it doesn't handle compound targets (webhook + pd) properly. Preparing a rollback patch.

2026-03-11 16:45 - Martin O'Neill (SRE): Patch applied to staging that preserves nested target arrays (branch: fix/retention-preserve-escalations). Running extended rollforward test. No data loss observed in staging after test run.

2026-03-12 08:13 - Customer (BrightLens Support Contact - Mark Ellis): Confirmed we received a test notification post-fix and trace links restored. Requesting timeline of root cause and mitigation for production.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Scheduling production patch window and follow-up postmortem; customer notified about planned maintenance at 2026-03-13 01:00 UTC.
resolution: Mitigation: Rolled back migration step 'normalize_targets' in production retention worker and applied a patch to preserve existing 'escalationTargets' and 'tracehookParams' arrays (PR #2334). Workaround for impacted customers: re-save affected alert rules in console to repopulate UI caches. Root cause: migration assumed a flattened target mapping and dropped nested recipient lists when encountering non-legacy metadata shapes. Follow-up: postmortem and hardened migration tests added to pipeline; add guards in retention worker to avoid in-place mutation of alert documents without a transactional backup. Production rollback scheduled on 2026-03-13 01:00 UTC; customer notified.
follow_up_actions: Create postmortem page and link to incident BL-INC-20260310-01
Add unit + integration tests for migration pipeline covering compound escalation targets
Run an org-scoped dry-run on retention jobs that output delta report before applying changes (build feature request)
Notify customers in similar cohorts and provide remediation script to restore tracehook tokens if needed
